article.story: MEXICO CITY -- — Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers offense turned the much ballyhooed matchup between one of the game's top offenses and the stingiest defenses into a one-sided affair. Purdy carved up Minnesota with three touchdown passes in the first half and the 49ers beat the Vikings 35-10 Sunday night in a matchup of NFC powerhouses. “You have to be aggressive and don’t second-guess yourself,” Purdy said. “Obviously try to read it out the best you can, but when you have players that can go get the ball, allow them to go and make plays. I just feel like our guys did that around me today. It wasn’t a one-man show. It was a really good team effort." The game played before a raucous pro-49ers crowd at historic Estadio Azteca was billed as a matchup between one of the league's most dangerous offenses in the 49ers (9-1) against a defense for the Vikings (7-3) that had rattled quarterbacks all season with an aggressive blitz package. Coordinator Brian Flores' schemes didn't work at all against Purdy, who torched the Minnesota defense for three touchdown drives on the Niners' first four possessions. “He was so good. He was quick, he was confident, he threw strikes,” said tight end George Kittle, who caught two TD passes. “He’s playing with confidence, he understands the offense, he is confident in the offense. He knows the offense. When he goes out there he just has this aura in the huddle.” San Francisco built a 28-10 halftime lead thanks to Purdy's stellar play and a pick-6 by Ji'Ayir Brown against Kirk Cousins. The Niners added the exclamation point in the second half with a 98-yard touchdown drive that featured “MVP!” chants for Purdy and was capped by Christian McCaffrey's 6-yard run that made it 35-10 early in the fourth quarter. Purdy finished 21 for 26 for 255 yards and a 146 passer rating that was more than double the league-low 69.5 rating that Minnesota entered the game allowing. “Seemed like he played a lot better than a lot of other guys have versus them, because not many people play that good versus that defense,” coach Kyle Shanahan said. “There’s a reason for that. It’s a huge challenge. It was hard looking at it all week. Brock didn’t get rattled, which he really never does. I think it says a lot about Brock.” Cousins lost for the second time in three weeks against the Niners, also throwing a pick-6 in Week 9 for the Raiders in his final start before being traded back to Minnesota. He became the first player ever to throw a pick-6 for two teams against the same opponent in a season. Cousins went 26 for 38 for 235 yards and was unable to follow up his winning performance last week for Minnesota at Green Bay. But the biggest reason was that the defense that dominated all season got picked apart. “There’s no group that I have more confidence in than not only those players on defense and that coaching staff,” Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said. “There’s just no really other way to put it. We just got beat tonight. They made some plays. I think the quarterback’s really good and they got a bunch of really good players and they execute at a really high level.” The 49ers set the tone early, easily moving down the field on a seven-play, 72-yard drive to open the game. Purdy completed all four of his passes for 55 yards, capped by a 17-yard touchdown to Kittle. After getting stopped on the second drive, Purdy scored on the next two possessions. He threw an 8-yard touchdown pass to Kittle to make it 14-7 and then a 4-yarder to Mike Evans that made it 21-10. Brown then intercepted Cousins on the next play from scrimmage and returned it 18 yards for the score that broke the game open. “The backside safety made a great play,” Cousins said. “I need to feel him and progress and not try to fit it in there.” Vikings try a fair catch kick The international crowd almost got to see one of the rarest plays in the NFL when the Vikings called for a fair catch at their own 40 with 3 seconds left in the first half. Connell sent out Will Reichard for a fair catch kick, with the teams lined up like a kickoff with no rush. The 71-yard attempt — which would have eclipsed the NFL record of 68 yards set by Cam Little last season — came up just short. There has been only one successful fair catch kick in the last 50 seasons, with Cameron Dicker making a 57-yarder for the Chargers against Denver in 2024. Teams take divergent approaches to altitude The teams took drastically different approaches to prepare for the game, which was played at more than 7,300 feet (2,220 meters) above sea level. The 49ers spent the week training at the Air Force Academy in Colorado — at an altitude of more than 7,000 feet — to acclimate. The Vikings stayed home but had players use a special elevation room for workouts during the last few weeks that mirrors conditions 9,000 or more feet above sea level. Injuries Vikings: LT Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) left the game briefly in the first half and then for good in the fourth quarter. 49ers: RT Colton McKivitz left in the second quarter with a fractured and dislocated left ankle. Up next Vikings: Host Atlanta next Sunday. 49ers: Host Seattle next Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
